summary: Shūei Tsuboi (1914–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested 1963, 1972) and was an editorial board member for Bukkyō Bunka Kenkyū.

Shūichi Katō (1919–2008) worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the First Higher School, University of Tokyo (Dr. med. by 1950), and University of Paris, he held posts at Sophia University, Ritsumeikan University, and the University of British Columbia.

Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma. He also studied under multiple traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala, U Sajjanasāra, and U Sāsana.

Sibani Dasgupta is an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and completed a doctorate at the University of Calcutta in 1954 under Sushil Kumar De, having also studied under Rajendra Chandra Hazra.

Sibnath Sarma is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He worked at the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Gauhati University (attested 1999–2012).
Sibraj Chetry is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies under Sibnath Sarma. He was attested as a lecturer of philosophy at North Lakhimpur College in 2012.

Sicheng Liang (1901–1972) was an archaeology and history scholar. He studied at Tsinghua University and the University of Pennsylvania School of Design before holding a post at Peking University from circa 1952 to 1972.

Siegfried Goldschmidt (1844–1884) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, Göttingen, and Tübingen (PhD 1867) under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth, later serving as an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg in 1881.

Siegfried Lienhard (1924–2011) was an Indologist. He studied at Vienna, Paris, and Stockholm, and held professorships at Kiel University (1962–1968) and Stockholm University (1968–1990), also serving as Secretary General of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~1973–1994).

Siglinde Dietz is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar who received her PhD from the University of Bonn in 1980 under Michael Hahn. She held a post at the University of Göttingen (attested 1990).
Signe Cohen is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Ludo Rocher and serves as a professor at the University of Missouri.
Signe Howell (1942–2025) studied at SOAS University of London and the University of Oxford. A specialist in religious studies, she was appointed professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.

Silvio Vita (1954–2023) worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology, studying at Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton. He taught at Naples "L'Orientale" (1992–2001) and Rome (2006–2012), and directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~1999–2021).

Simo Parpola (born 1943) is an Assyriologist and linguist who studied at the University of Helsinki (PhD), the Pontifical Biblical Institute, and the British Museum. He held professorships at the University of Chicago (1977–1979) and the University of Helsinki (1978).
Simon Cubelic is an Indologist and historian attested in 2018 at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and as an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica.
Simon P. James is a philosophy and religious studies scholar who held posts at Durham University as a tutor (attested 2001) and lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
Singhathon Narāsabho is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed a PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

Siniruddha Dash (born 1955) is an Indologist and linguist. He served as Director at the University of Madras (2000–2014), the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 2013), and the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation.

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala (1942–2021) was an archaeologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, the University of London, and Harvard University under Raymond Allchin. He served as Director General of the Department of Archaeology, Sri Lanka (~1992–2001).

Sisir Roy is a philosophy scholar who studied under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts as a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute and at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (both attested 2009).
